correctness.rationale: The Gaussian two-contact variance recursion gives an exact stationary bivariate law. Wick fourth moments yield the work variance; the Gaussian quadrant formula gives the exact positive-work probability and its strictly monotone transformation of reliability. Differentiating squared reliability gives a positive prefactor times one explicit cubic, whose derivative and endpoint signs prove one and only one global optimizer. Exact evaluation at the mean-optimal split proves strictly unequal durations. Positive-temperature boundaries and both asymptotics are derived. Standalone symbolic and deterministic checks from verify.py corroborate critical identities; they are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The original exact optimization theorem treats fixed combined hot/cold thermal contact time in a periodically stationary overdamped Gaussian Otto cycle with equal coordinate decay rates. Inspection of Zheng, Hänggi and Poletti (2016) finds bath time optimization for mean work and efficiency in a different quantum Otto setup, not exact one-cycle reliability and success. Iida, Negoro and Yamada (2022) derive second moments for continuously breathing Brownian potentials and offer a Gaussian approximation to work success, not exact optimum of bath-contact split. Shastri and Venkatesh (arXiv:2204.04782, 2022) optimize reliability versus unitary compression/expansion stroke asymmetry and fix bath-contact split in principal calculations; their conclusion calls for a follow-up study of bath-time asymmetry on fluctuations. These statements do not imply the globally unique cubic cold-biased optimum and its exact probability co-optimization without new analysis. The non-coverage is limited to the material inspected and does not establish absolute priority.
residual_risks: A general covariance/optimal-control result outside the inspected literature may imply the cubic allocation without identical wording.

Single-cycle versus cumulative-work reliability, exact probability versus normal approximation, and equality of relaxation rates are essential scope distinctions; unrecognized reductions could change priority.
Scientific novelty is assessed on the inspected evidence, not independently certified.

value.rationale: The finite-time hot/cold dwell allocation is a motivated design question for fluctuating thermal engines. Unlike standard mean-work optimization, the exact optimal reliability/success criterion strictly favors the colder bath for every parameter in a natural equal-relaxation-rate subfamily; its unique cubic, strict separation, and fast/slow asymptotics provide a complete structural result. Deriving exact non-Gaussian sign probability avoids the normal-proxy approximation in the literature. Does not claim relevance beyond the explicitly restricted model.
